narr: With the subtropical high pressure system centered over the Four Corners Region, the flow across the region was from the southeast. Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours, particularly over Pima County in southeast AZ, and were steered northwestward towards western Maricopa County with additional activity developing from outflow boundaries. The combination of MLCAPE values of 500-1000 J/KG and DCAPE values in excess of 1500 J/KG, resulted in an environment conducive to strong to severe downburst winds. Some of the thunderstorm activity was also slow moving, resulting isolated flash flooding, with the area of Cruff Wash south of Buckeye reaching bankfull and resulting in flooding along low-water crossings.
ev: According to the Maricopa County Flood Control District Gauge located at Cruff Wash, water levels rose above the alarm level stage of 2.5 feet at around 1952MST and crested at 3.91 feet, which is above the bank full level stage of 3.88 feet, at around 2015MST. Water levels fell below alarm stage at around 2105MST. Based on the information of problem areas produced by the Maricopa County Flood Control District, flooding was likely along the low water crossing of Agua Caliente Road located above 2 miles downstream of the gauge. No damages nor injuries were reported.
lsr: Cruff Wash reached alarm stage around 752pm and crested at bankfull at 815pm. Time estimated for flow to reach Agua Caliente Rd and require closure.
